claims.claim: Direct variable cost: fully avoidable; it ends with the last C shipment

Shared cost that stays: regulatory documentation and plant depreciation, spread by historical engineering hours

evidence: Direct contribution margin, FY2026: Connector C 0.6333; Connector A 0.5; Connector D 0.5; Connector B 0.4222

18% of Vesper's connector sales

evidence: Contribution effect of exiting connector C in Q2 2027, first full year, no migration to D, $M: C contribution lost -3.8; Avoidable fixed cost saved -0.4 [as charted]; Bundle penalties -2.1; First-year effect -5.5

claims.claim: moving C customers to D would win back at most $750K a year
evidence: $6.0M C sales × 25% ceiling × 50% D incremental contribution = $750K

claims.claim: Even the best case loses money every year

slides.title: Replacing C's contribution would take $6.8M of new D sales, more than C sells today and far beyond D's capacity

claims.claim: Replacing C's contribution would take $6.8M of new D sales
evidence: $3.4M contribution lost each year on exit: C's $3.8M direct contribution less $0.4M avoidable fixed cost
÷ 50% incremental contribution on each extra dollar of D sales at existing capacity (Finance)
= $6.8M of new D sales needed every year just to stand still

claims.claim: D cannot fill that gap, even if every C customer agreed to switch
evidence: D can take only $1.5M of additional revenue at present capacity; the requirement is 4.5 times that
C sells $6.0M a year: if every C dollar moved to D, the $3.0M gained would still fall short of the $3.4M lost
The portfolio team's 25% migration ceiling, from three sales interviews, would use all of D's spare capacity
Adapters and validation are customer-specific, and no substitute for C is validated across every hospital model

evidence: 64% of the 14 major hospital relationships specify a bundle with C, A and B

claims.claim: D needs customer-specific adapters and validation
evidence: 0 substitutes for C validated across every hospital model
Qualification and clinical documentation come first
Each account needs its own validated replacement

slides.title: What the evidence against C shows
The renewal gap of 9 percentage points shows who buys C; it does not prove that C drives customers away

claims.claim: The claim rests on a snapshot, not a test
evidence: −9 pp renewal gap against non-C accounts
The CEO's scatter plot compares hospital renewal rates by product mix
It shows that C accounts renew less often, not why
No account in the sample is seen before and after a change in C

claims.claim: C buyers differ in ways that predict churn on their own
evidence: Smaller hospitals buy C disproportionately
C is concentrated in accounts running legacy equipment
C accounts get lower customer-success coverage
Each of these can lower renewal whether or not C is in the order

claims.claim: Before acting on it, test it like for like
evidence: Compare C and non-C accounts of the same size, equipment and coverage
Track renewal where coverage rises but C stays
Until then, read the gap as a coverage signal, not a product verdict

claims.claim: The evidence neither proves nor rules out a C effect
evidence: Renewal comparison from the CEO's scatter plot of hospital renewal rates by product mix; no account-level data in the pack

slides.title: The real service problem, hidden by C's dashboard, is bundle fill of 91% against the 95% the contracts require

claims.claim: The dashboard measures C, the contracts measure bundles
evidence: Fill rate: C on-time fill (dashboard) 0.98; Bundle fill, nine bundle customers 0.91
Contract minimum 95%

claims.claim: Dashboard figure: counts C as on time even when a bundle ships late because A or B is missing
evidence: The dashboard excludes late bundle deliveries whenever A or B is the missing item

claims.claim: Bundle fill: what the nine bundle contracts measure, and it is below the minimum today
Exit does not fix it: without C, bundles that specify C cannot be filled at all
Fix bundle-level fill before the two renewals close; it breaches the contracts with or without C

slides.title: Redesigning C is the only option that adds contribution while staying within the cash limit and keeping every bundle

claims.claim: Redesigning C is the only option that adds contribution while staying within the cash limit and keeping every bundle
evidence: Exit C in Q2 2027 | −$3.4M | $2.1M | Broken for 9 of 14 major hospitals unless they consent | Reject: largest loss, and penalties exceed the cash limit
Retain C without changes | No change | None | Kept, but bundle fill stays at 91% | Fallback if the pilot fails; price pressure on C remains

Redesign C, gated on a two-site pilot | $1,250K | $550K | Kept; four-month validation, two customers may need requalification | Recommended / Uses $550K of the $0.9M cash limit and lifts C's contribution
Orderly sunset in 2029 | None until 2029 | None | Exit timed to expiring agreements, if renewals allow it | Keep open; decide in 2028 with D and pilot evidence
Exit: −$2.65M a year in the best case, if 25% of C sales move to D; redesign savings are Manufacturing Engineering's estimate at current volume

claims.claim: The pack does not quantify the D work the design team would defer during the four-month redesign

slides.title: The redesign recovers its cost within a year as long as savings at scale reach 44% of the engineering estimate

claims.claim: The redesign recovers its cost within a year as long as savings at scale reach 44% of the engineering estimate
evidence: $550K one-time redesign cost: qualification, external sterilization validation and fixtures
÷ $1,250K annual direct savings at current volume (Manufacturing Engineering estimate)
= 44% of the estimated savings is enough to recover the cost in the first year of savings

claims.claim: Four conditions decide whether the payback holds
evidence: At the full estimate, the cost is recovered 5.3 months after the four-month validation, about 9.3 months from the start
The savings equal 57% of C's direct variable cost and are unproven at scale, so the pilot must confirm them before line conversion

Four months of the design team on C delay D work; that cost is not quantified and is not netted out

normalized.recommendation: Reject the Q2 2027 exit and approve the $550K C redesign, with line conversion gated on the two-site pilot; renew both bundle agreements with C included and notice terms that allow a 2029 exit; fix bundle-level fill to the 95% minimum; and decide on a sunset in 2028 with D adapter acceptance and pilot evidence.

Fallback if the pilot fails; price pressure on C remains. No contribution change, no cash; bundles kept, but bundle fill stays at 91%.

alternatives_considered.treatment: Recommended / Uses $550K of the $0.9M cash limit and lifts C's contribution ($1,250K a year; four-month validation, two customers may need requalification).
